newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan protesters demand premier's resignation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan protesters demand premier's resignation.

text.p: Activists on Saturday demonstrated for the third time in three weeks outside the Presidential Office to denounce President Lee Teng-hui and demand the resignation of Premier Lien Chan.
In front of barred-wire barricades and a thousand riot police, hundreds of protesters unfurled banners telling Lee and Lien to "get lost".
"With the social order deteriorating daily, what else can we expect from Premier Lien other than to ask him to get lost," shouted an activist through a loudspeaker.
Protest organiser Lee Tien-chien of the Humanistic Education Foundation said the demonstration would run through the night to voice "utmost discontent" with the government.
"We decided to hold this protest because we feel that the government just turned a deaf ear to our demands in our earlier protests," he said.
More than 50,000 people marched on the Presidential Office on May 4 and May 18 to protest at investigators' failure to solve a string of murders.
"We want President Lee Teng-hui to acknowledge mistakes to his policies, including appointing Lien Chan as premier," he added.

Lien and his cabinet have faced fierce criticism over numerous unsolved crimes, including the gangland-style execution of a county magistrate and seven associates in his home and the kidnap and murder of the daughter of a prominent actress.
To regain public confidence, Lien has offered to give up the premiership after constitutional reforms are adopted in July.
